lessons.instruction: When an exclusion clause mentions a money threshold (for example monthly pension Rs.10,000 or more) but the allowed fact is a boolean whose name already encodes that threshold, write that fact as eq false for the excluded group. Do not invent gte/lte numeric operators on that boolean field.
lessons.when_to_apply: Exclusion clauses about pension or similar thresholds mapped to boolean facts such as pension_at_least_10000_excluding_stated_grades.
lessons.review_reason: Accuracy fix for PMKISAN-GUIDELINES-2020-4.1(b)(iv): model often wrote gte 10000 on a boolean exclusion fact.

lessons.instruction: When a clause says "aged N and above", write one inclusive lower-bound rule (gte N) and no upper bound. When a clause says a person's "names are on the ... list", map the condition to the list-membership fact (`name_on_bpl_list`, eq true), not to a card-shown fact. The two BPL facts are different and must not be used interchangeably.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any inclusion clause that states an "and above" age threshold together with a condition that the person's name appears on a list.

lessons.instruction: When a clause specifies categories of individuals who are ineligible, ensure the rule reflects that these individuals are not qualified by setting the value to false, rather than true.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any clause that lists specific categories of individuals or groups who do not qualify for a benefit or scheme.
lessons.review_reason: Clear and general: an excluded group is written as false, not true.

lessons.instruction: When the clause text contains more than one sentence under a single clause_id, read every sentence and write a rule for each condition named in any of them. Do not stop after the first sentence (for example age bounds) when a later sentence adds citizenship or a savings-bank requirement.
lessons.when_to_apply: Inclusion clauses whose supplied text spans multiple sentences or lists several independent eligibility conditions.
lessons.review_reason: Accuracy fix for APY-IN-ELIGIBILITY-01 after case-text assembly joined all unique source_text lines: model must use the full multi-sentence clause block, not only the age sentence.

lessons.instruction: When an inclusion clause states several conditions across one or more sentences (for example an age range, citizenship, and having a savings bank account), write a separate rule for each condition. Do not stop after the age bounds.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any inclusion clause that combines age limits with other eligibility conditions such as citizenship or account ownership.
lessons.review_reason: Accuracy fix for APY-IN-ELIGIBILITY-01: model often omitted citizen and savings-bank rules after extracting age.

lessons.instruction: When a clause gives an age range written as "X to Y years", write two separate rules: an inclusive lower bound (gte X) and an inclusive upper bound (lte Y). Do not write the range as one rule. Map a "family falls under Below Poverty Line" condition to the BPL card fact (`bpl_card_shown`), not to a list-membership fact.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any inclusion clause that combines a category (for example, a widow), an age range, and a BPL condition on the family.
